capture.final_message:
Treat the two conjuncts independently.

- For the open immersion \(f:X\to Y\), the open \(U\subseteq X\) and its image \(f(U)\subseteq Y\) define isomorphic open subschemes. Reduce both `IsAffineOpen` assertions to affineness of these restrictions, then use invariance of affineness under scheme isomorphism.

- For the second conjunct, use the standard finite-type fiber criterion for local quasi-finiteness. Identify the underlying space of the scheme-theoretic fiber \(X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\) with \(f^{-1}(\{y\})\). Under `LocallyOfFiniteType`, local quasi-finiteness is equivalent to every fiber being zero-dimensional; a finite-type scheme over a field is zero-dimensional exactly when its spectrum is discrete (equivalently, its coordinate rings are Artinian). Thus the stated discreteness condition is precisely the fiberwise criterion.

The locally finite-type assumption is essential in the converse: it turns zero-dimensional/discrete fibers into finite, hence quasi-finite, fibers.
